agent: claude -p (fresh context, saw only skill names and descriptions)

descriptions.skill-smith: Build a new Skill Foundry skill from the template, as ten layers, portable for other people, so it passes the factory linter, evals and review and has a recorded real run. Use when asked for a new skill or to turn a repeated workflow into a skill. Do not use for a typo fix in an existing skill.
descriptions.figure-craft: Draws a detailed isometric figure that explains how a thing works, from the goal the user states, with a token palette, a shared iso engine and a geometry, layout and detail lint. Use for any request for an explanatory diagram, technical illustration or interactive explainer of an object or system. Do not use for data charts, photos, logos, UI mockups or decorative art.
descriptions.changelog-writer: Turns a list of merged changes into one CHANGELOG.md entry in the Skill Foundry format. Use when asked to write a changelog entry, release notes or a version bump note for a skill. Do not use for commit messages, long-form docs or marketing copy; use copy-tight for wording.
descriptions.copy-tight: Rewrites UI copy (buttons, labels, errors, empty states, tooltips) to be short and plain without changing meaning. Use when asked to "shorten this copy", "make this plain", "tighten this text" or when a UI string is too wordy. Do not use for long-form docs, blog posts, translation or changelog entries; use changelog-writer for those.
descriptions.test-planner: Derives a numbered regression checklist, grouped by area, from a change description or a diff, so the team knows what to retest and nothing outside the change is added. Use when asked "what should we retest after this change?" or "give me a regression checklist for this diff". Do not use to write test code, to review a diff for bugs, or to plan tests for features the change does not describe; answer those in the chat instead.
descriptions.ui-polish: Runs a final polish pass on the HTML and CSS (or JSX) of a finished UI, fixing spacing, type, contrast, visual hierarchy, interactive states and layout against fixed numeric rules, and returns the numbered fixes plus the polished code with every word of text kept. Use when asked for a "final polish", a "pixel pass", or to "make this screen look cleaner" on code the user pastes. Do not use to design a new screen from scratch, to rewrite UI copy (use copy-tight), or for a full accessibility audit.
